policy_title: Deepen Devolution Across England and Support Local Government
stated: Labour will enact landmark devolution legislation, deepening settlements for existing Combined Authorities and widening devolution to more areas. Local leaders will gain new powers over transport, adult education, skills, housing, planning, and employment support. The party will require Local Growth Plans, review Combined Authority governance, provide multi-year funding settlements to councils, and improve public service workers' living standards.

source.quote: Labour will transfer power out of Westminster, and into our communities, with landmark devolution legislation to take back control. In England, Labour will deepen devolution settlements for existing Combined Authorities. We will also widen devolution to more areas, encouraging local authorities to come together and take on new powers. Towns and cities will be able to take hold of the tools they need to pursue growth, create jobs, and improve living standards. Local areas will be able to gain new powers over transport, adult education and skills, housing and planning, and employment support. At the centre of our approach is a new statutory requirement for Local Growth Plans that cover towns and cities across the country. Labour will review the governance arrangements for Combined Authorities to unblock decision making. To provide greater stability, a Labour government will give councils multiyear funding settlements and end wasteful competitive bidding. Labour will act to improve public service workers’ living standards throughout the parliament, and ensure any independent mechanisms have the confidence of all involved.

bearing_set.reason: Explicit new local powers over housing and planning mean decisions on supply, permissions, and affordability are materially shifted, warranting a real verdict on whether homes get built and at what cost.
Devolving adult education and skills to local leaders directly alters funding flows, curricula priorities, and access to further education and apprenticeships for local populations.

Devolved employment support powers affect job-entry quality and in-work progression for local residents, and the explicit commitment to improve public service workers' living standards directly touches wages and conditions for a large workforce.

Required Local Growth Plans plus devolved transport, skills and employment levers constitute a deliberate mechanism for improving local productivity, business investment and economic opportunity — the core indicators of this outcome.

The explicit widening of devolution 'to more areas' targets regions currently without Combined Authority powers, with a concrete mechanism for narrowing the regional inequality component of this outcome's indicators.

membership_note: This is a broad multi-sector devolution package with direct levers across housing, skills, work and local economic development; five genuine bearings emerge from separately-named powers rather than inflated coverage. Democratic-rights effects (O9) were considered but judged incidental to the substantive life-outcome effects scored here. Fiscal effects of multi-year settlements were considered for O12 but the policy does not signal additional aggregate spending — it repackages existing funding flows — so O12 does not clear the non-negligible bar.
